world.title: ACWECA: National Disability Dialogue Conference 2026
world.description:
Sr. Teresa Banda
The Catholic Relief Services (CRS), Association of Consecrated Women in Eastern and Central Africa (ACWECA), and Association of Sisterhoods of Kenya (AOSK) actively took part in the National Disability Dialogue Forum organized by the National Council for Persons with Disabilities (NCPWD). The event, held from 13th to 14th May 2026 at the Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development (KICD), brought together over 1,000 participants including government representatives, faith-based organizations, development partners, caregivers and advocates for disability inclusion.
The dialogue, themed “From Policy to Practice: Co-creating an Inclusive and Prosperous Society by Reimagining Care Systems,” provided a critical platform for reflection, knowledge sharing and engagement among stakeholders committed to disability inclusion and strengthened care systems. Engagement from various organizations highlighted the growing contribution of faith-based institutions in advancing inclusive care systems and supporting vulnerable groups, especially children and caregivers. Throughout the forum, stakeholders were given an opportunity to present and showcase their initiatives, helping to connect policy discussions with practical community-based interventions. Such interactions emphasized the value of partnerships and collective action in strengthening inclusive caregiving systems.
Insightful presentations further demonstrated how initiatives such as the SCORE ECD project, supported by the Conrad N. Hilton Foundation, are translating ideas into meaningful community impact through strengthened caregiving practices and the promotion of inclusive child development at the grassroots level. In addition, the sessions created space for caregivers and practitioners to share their lived experiences, shedding light on critical gaps within care systems and stressing the need to move beyond policy frameworks toward practical, community-driven solutions.
Particular emphasis was placed on the experiences of caregivers of children with disabilities, whose moving testimonies highlighted challenges such as limited access to specialized services, inadequate financial support, stigma and discrimination, harassment, emotional and psychological strain and insufficient training on disability-specific care. Discussions also brought focus to domestic support personnel caring for children with disabilities, recognizing them as a vulnerable group that often works with limited recognition, social protection and support systems. The conversations strongly emphasized the urgent need for more inclusive policies, stronger support structures and greater recognition of caregivers and support workers within community care systems.
Amidst these challenges, the discussions highlighted the resilience and commitment of caregivers as well as the vital role they continue to play in nurturing and supporting children with disabilities. The dialogue further emphasized the importance of collaboration among various stakeholders including government institutions, faith-based organizations, development partners and other key actors in building inclusive and sustainable care systems.
Participation by CRS, ACWECA and AOSK not only created an opportunity to showcase their impactful work but also strengthened partnerships and enhanced opportunities for greater coordination, collaboration and visibility within the disability inclusion space. Ultimately, the dialogue reaffirmed that reimagining care systems requires collective action inclusive approaches and a strong commitment to translating policies into meaningful practice to ensure that no child or caregiver is left behind.

world.title: MALAWI: Chikwawa Prelate Urges Youth to Desist from Mob Justice Linked to “Myth”
world.description:
Luke Bisani
The Prelate of the Diocese of Chikwawa, Rt. Rev. Peter Martin Musikuwa, has urged young people under his diocese to refrain from mob justice linked to the myth of mysteriously disappearing of private parts.
Speaking this week after a requiem Mass for one of the victims, Alan Mashonga, Bishop Musikuwa appealed to the youth who are reportedly at the forefront of the attacks to stop taking the law into their own hands.
“I urge all young people, because from the look of things, it is the youth who are in the forefront of punishing people suspected of having a hand in the alleged disappearance of men’s private parts. Let us all seek redress from the relevant authorities,” said Bishop Musikuwa.
Over the past two weeks, the country has witnessed growing panic over claims of people being dismembered and their private parts mysteriously missing, a myth believed to have originated in Zambia.
The attacks linked to the claims have so far claimed eight lives in the districts of Chikwawa District and Nsanje District.
Despite sensitization campaigns led by the Minister of Local Government and Rural Development, Ben Phiri, Deputy Inspector General of Police Noel Kayira, Chikwawa District Commissioner Frank Mkandawire, Paramount Chief Lundu, and legislators from Nsanje, cases of mob attacks continue to be reported, with at least one new incident recorded this week.

science.title: Environmental fee-to-tax reform policy driving corporate green governance performance: the sustainable path to reducing carbon emission intensity
science.description: Against the backdrop of growing resource constraints and ecological degradation, green development has emerged as the core pathway for advancing sustainable economic transformation. Using data from Chinese A-share listed companies on the Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Exchanges between 2010 and 2023, this study examines the impact and underlying mechanisms of the environmental fee-to-tax reform (EPFT) on corporate green governance performance (GGP). We find that EPFT significantly improves corporate GGP and this positive effect exhibits clear heterogeneity. It is stronger in non-resource-based cities while insignificant in resource-based cities, where stronger local environmental regulation can offset the policy’s ineffectiveness. In terms of industry characteristics, the effect is significant in non-heavy-polluting and capital-intensive industries but insignificant in heavy-polluting and non-capital-intensive industries. For managerial characteristics, the effect is concentrated in firms led by executives with environmental education or work experience, particularly CEOs, while it is insignificant for those without such backgrounds. Mechanistically, EPFT enhances GGP by alleviating financing constraints, attracting green investors, and promoting green innovation. Furthermore, EPFT strengthens the spillover effects of GGP on corporate ESG performance and CSR fulfillment, and ultimately reduces carbon emission intensity by elevating GGP levels. These findings provide empirical support and actionable insights for optimizing the environmental tax system and advancing regional sustainable development.
